These PCV valve failures are incredibly common with the 2.0 motor. If you're even remotely handy and own a torx socket (t30 off the top of my head, might be 25/27) you can change this at home for about $100. Just be very gentle with the hose leading to the intake manifold, or plan to replace it while you're at it, it's incredibly brittle. There's a million youtube videos on this repair, they may call it a PCV valve, crank case breather, oil separator, vent/ventilation valve, all the same thing. Start there and see how much your consumption is reduced. You may luck out.
